writeup: TIC 182536219 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 9.81 days, detected in TESS photometry through automated analysis. The primary eclipse produces a 2.31 percent dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal registers at high confidence in the data, with a BLS detection significance of 170.1 and pixel-level difference imaging confirming a peak signal-to-noise of 15.9. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths - a pattern suggesting the true orbital period may be twice the initial measurement. Pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this uncertainty, but the depth variation represents an open question about the system's true configuration.
